editorial.headline: Independent Dental Practice: Open Nationally, Address-Checked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers independent dental care and treatment by dentists, open across every listed business scale with full national foreign-ownership access.
editorial.body:
Independent dental practice is defined here with useful precision: it is the provision of dental health-care and treatment services carried out independently by dentists. The centre of gravity is the professional activity itself—dental care and treatment delivered by a dentist in independent practice. That focus keeps the classification clear: this is not a broad description of health services, but a specific activity rooted in the independent work of dentists.

The code is open at every listed scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That range matters because the record does not reserve the activity for one business size. Its commercial frame can therefore sit across the full stated scale spectrum, while the underlying activity remains the same: independent dental care and treatment undertaken by dentists. The scale classification describes the available range; the scope describes the work that gives the code its identity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, the record places no foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity at the national level. For a foreign-owned structure, that is the governing national position supplied by the record: the activity is open and may carry up to 100% foreign ownership. The relevant source is the cited Presidential Regulations, rather than an inferred rule drawn from adjacent activities or general assumptions about health-related practice.

Bali requires a more exact reading, but not a dramatic one. The Bali classification is recorded as medium-high/high risk and is not blocked by the province-wide moratorium. A foreign investor is therefore not shut out from registering this activity in Bali by that moratorium. The record nevertheless calls for verification by address. That is an important distinction: national openness and Bali's absence of a moratorium block support the activity's availability, while the address remains a stated point to verify. The accurate conclusion is neither a blanket Bali prohibition nor an unconditional promise. It is an activity open nationally to full foreign ownership and not moratorium-blocked in Bali, subject to the record's address-specific verification.
